{{Short description|Mathematical theory}}
In [[mathematics]], the '''Chern–Weil homomorphism''' is a basic construction in '''Chern–Weil theory''' that computes [[topology|topological]] invariants of [[vector bundle]]s and [[principal bundle]]s on a [[smooth manifold]] ''M'' in terms of [[Connection (mathematics)|connections]] and [[curvature]] representing classes in the [[de Rham cohomology]] rings of ''M''. That is, the theory forms a bridge between the areas of [[algebraic topology]] and [[differential geometry]]. It was developed in the late 1940s by [[Shiing-Shen Chern]] and [[André Weil]], in the wake of proofs of the [[generalized Gauss–Bonnet theorem]]. This theory was an important step in the theory of [[characteristic class]]es.

Let ''G'' be a real or complex [[Lie group]] with [[Lie algebra]] {{nowrap|<math>\mathfrak g</math>,}} and let <math>\Complex[\mathfrak g]</math> denote the algebra of <math>\Complex</math>-valued [[Polynomials on vector spaces|polynomial]]s on <math>\mathfrak g</math> (exactly the same argument works if we used <math>\R</math> instead of {{nowrap|<math>\Complex</math>).}} Let <math>\Complex[\mathfrak g]^G</math> be the [[fixed-point subring|subalgebra of fixed points]] in <math>\Complex[\mathfrak g]</math> under the [[adjoint representation of a Lie group|adjoint action]] of ''G''; that is, the subalgebra consisting of all polynomials ''f'' such that  <math>f(\operatorname{Ad}_g x) = f(x)</math>, for all ''g'' in ''G'' and ''x'' in <math>\mathfrak{g}</math>,

Given a [[principal bundle|principal G-bundle]] ''P'' on ''M'', there is an associated homomorphism of <math>\Complex</math>-algebras,
:<math>\Complex[\mathfrak g]^{G} \to H^*(M; \Complex)</math>,
called the '''Chern–Weil homomorphism''', where on the right cohomology is [[de Rham cohomology]].  This homomorphism is obtained by taking invariant polynomials in the curvature of any connection on the given bundle.  If ''G'' is either compact  or semi-simple, then the [[cohomology ring]] of the [[classifying space]] for ''G''-bundles, <math>BG</math>, is isomorphic to the algebra <math>\Complex[\mathfrak g]^{G}</math> of invariant polynomials:
:<math>H^*(BG; \Complex) \cong \Complex[\mathfrak g]^{G}.</math>
(The cohomology ring of ''BG'' can still be given in the de Rham sense:
:<math>H^k(BG; \Complex) = \varinjlim \operatorname{ker} (d\colon \Omega^k(B_jG) \to \Omega^{k+1}(B_jG))/\operatorname{im} d.</math>
when <math>BG = \varinjlim B_jG</math> and <math>B_jG</math> are manifolds.)

==Definition of the homomorphism==
Choose any [[connection form]] ω in ''P'', and let Ω be the associated [[curvature form]]; i.e., {{nowrap|<math>\Omega = D\omega</math>,}} the [[exterior covariant derivative]] of ω. If <math>f\in\mathbb C[\mathfrak g]^G</math> is a [[homogeneous polynomial]] function of degree&nbsp;''k''; i.e., <math>f(a x) = a^k f(x)</math> for any complex number ''a'' and ''x'' in {{nowrap|<math>\mathfrak g</math>,}} then, viewing ''f'' as a symmetric multilinear functional on <math display="inline">\prod_1^k \mathfrak{g}</math> (see the [[ring of polynomial functions]]), let <math>f(\Omega)</math>
be the (scalar-valued) 2''k''-form on ''P'' given by
:<math>f(\Omega)(v_1,\dots,v_{2k})=\frac{1}{(2k)!}\sum_{\sigma\in\mathfrak S_{2k}}\epsilon_\sigma f(\Omega(v_{\sigma(1)},v_{\sigma(2)}),\dots,\Omega(v_{\sigma(2k-1)}, v_{\sigma(2k)}))</math>
where ''v''<sub>''i''</sub> are tangent vectors to ''P'', <math>\epsilon_\sigma</math> is the sign of the permutation <math>\sigma</math> in the symmetric group on 2''k'' numbers <math>\mathfrak S_{2k}</math> (see [[Lie algebra-valued forms#Operations]] as well as [[Pfaffian]]).

If, moreover, ''f'' is invariant; i.e., <math>f(\operatorname{Ad}_g x) = f(x)</math>, then one can show that <math>f(\Omega)</math> is a [[Closed and exact differential forms|closed form]], it descends to a unique form on ''M'' and that the [[de Rham cohomology]] class of the form is independent of <math>\omega</math>. First, that <math>f(\Omega)</math> is a closed form follows from the next two lemmas:<ref>{{harvnb|Kobayashi|Nomizu|1969|loc=Ch. XII.}}</ref>

:Lemma 1: The form <math>f(\Omega)</math> on ''P'' descends to a (unique) form <math>\overline{f}(\Omega)</math> on ''M''; i.e., there is a form on ''M'' that pulls-back to <math>f(\Omega)</math>.
:Lemma 2: If a form of <math>\varphi</math> on ''P'' descends to a form on ''M'', then <math>d\varphi = D\varphi</math>.

Indeed, [[Bianchi's second identity]] says <math>D \Omega = 0</math> and, since ''D'' is a graded derivation, <math>D f(\Omega) = 0.</math> Finally, Lemma 1 says <math>f(\Omega)</math> satisfies the hypothesis of Lemma 2.

To see Lemma 2, let <math>\pi\colon P \to M</math> be the projection and ''h'' be the projection of <math>T_u P</math> onto the horizontal subspace. Then Lemma 2 is a consequence of the fact that <math>d \pi(h v) = d \pi(v)</math> (the kernel of <math>d \pi</math> is precisely the vertical subspace.) As for Lemma 1, first note
:<math>f(\Omega)(d R_g(v_1), \dots, d R_g(v_{2k})) = f(\Omega)(v_1, \dots, v_{2k}), \, R_g(u) = ug;</math>
which is because <math>R_g^* \Omega = \operatorname{Ad}_{g^{-1}} \Omega</math> and ''f'' is invariant. Thus, one can define <math>\overline{f}(\Omega)</math> by the formula:
:<math>\overline{f}(\Omega)(\overline{v_1}, \dots, \overline{v_{2k}}) = f(\Omega)(v_1, \dots, v_{2k}),</math>
where <math>v_i</math> are any lifts of <math>\overline{v_i}</math>: <math>d \pi(v_i) = \overline{v}_i</math>.

Next, we show that the de Rham cohomology class of <math>\overline{f}(\Omega)</math> on ''M'' is independent of a choice of connection.<ref>The argument for the independent of a choice of connection here is taken from: Akhil Mathew, Notes on Kodaira vanishing {{cite web|url=https://math.berkeley.edu/~amathew/kodaira.pdf |title=Archived copy |access-date=2014-12-11 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141217025038/https://math.berkeley.edu/~amathew/kodaira.pdf |archive-date=2014-12-17 }}. Kobayashi-Nomizu, the main reference, gives a more concrete argument.</ref> Let <math>\omega_0, \omega_1</math> be arbitrary connection forms on ''P'' and let <math>p\colon P \times \R \to P</math> be the projection. Put
:<math>\omega' = t \, p^* \omega_1 + (1 - t) \, p^* \omega_0</math>
where ''t'' is a smooth function on <math>P \times \mathbb{R}</math> given by <math>(x, s) \mapsto s</math>. Let <math>\Omega', \Omega_0, \Omega_1</math> be the curvature forms of <math>\omega', \omega_0, \omega_1</math>. Let <math>i_s: M \to M \times \mathbb{R}, \, x \mapsto (x, s)</math> be the inclusions. Then <math>i_0</math> is homotopic to <math>i_1</math>. Thus, <math>i_0^* \overline{f}(\Omega')</math> and <math>i_1^* \overline{f}(\Omega')</math> belong to the same de Rham cohomology class by the [[homotopy invariance of de Rham cohomology]]. Finally, by naturality and by uniqueness of descending,
:<math>i_0^* \overline{f}(\Omega') = \overline{f}(\Omega_0)</math>
and the same for <math>\Omega_1</math>. Hence, <math>\overline{f}(\Omega_0), \overline{f}(\Omega_1)</math> belong to the same cohomology class.

The construction thus gives the linear map: (cf. Lemma 1)
:<math>\Complex[\mathfrak g]^{G}_k \to H^{2k}(M; \Complex), \, f \mapsto \left[\overline{f}(\Omega)\right].</math>
In fact, one can check that the map thus obtained:
:<math>\Complex[\mathfrak g]^{G} \to H^*(M; \Complex)</math>
is an [[algebra homomorphism]].

== Example: Chern classes and Chern character ==
Let <math>G = \operatorname{GL}_n(\Complex)</math> and <math>\mathfrak{g} = \mathfrak{gl}_n(\Complex)</math> its Lie algebra. For each <math> x \in \mathfrak{g}</math>, we can consider its [[characteristic polynomial]] in ''t'':<ref>Editorial note: This definition is consistent with the reference except we have ''t'', which is ''t'' <sup>−1</sup> there. Our choice seems more standard and is consistent with our "[[Chern class]]" article.</ref>
:<math>\det \left( I - t{x \over 2 \pi i} \right) = \sum_{k=0}^n f_k(x) t^k,</math>
where ''i'' is the square root of -1. Then <math>f_k</math> are invariant polynomials on <math>\mathfrak{g}</math>, since the left-hand side of the equation is. The ''k''-th [[Chern class]] of a smooth complex-vector bundle ''E'' of rank ''n'' on a manifold ''M'':
:<math>c_k(E) \in H^{2k}(M, \Z)</math>
is given as the image of <math>f_k</math> under the Chern–Weil homomorphism defined by ''E'' (or more precisely the [[frame bundle]] of ''E''). If ''t'' = 1, then <math>\det \left(I - {x \over 2 \pi i} \right) = 1 + f_1(x) + \cdots + f_n(x)</math> is an invariant polynomial. The [[total Chern class]] of ''E'' is the image of this polynomial; that is,
:<math>c(E) = 1 + c_1(E) + \cdots + c_n(E).</math>

Directly from the definition, one can show that <math>c_j</math> and ''c'' given above satisfy the axioms of Chern classes. For example, for the Whitney sum formula, we consider
:<math>c_t(E) = [\det \left( I - t {\Omega / 2 \pi i} \right)],</math>
where we wrote <math>\Omega</math> for the [[curvature form|curvature 2-form]] on ''M'' of the vector bundle ''E'' (so it is the descendent of the curvature form on the frame bundle of ''E''). The Chern–Weil homomorphism is the same if one uses this <math>\Omega</math>. Now, suppose ''E'' is a direct sum of vector bundles <math>E_i</math>'s and <math>\Omega_i</math> the curvature form of <math>E_i</math> so that, in the matrix term, <math>\Omega</math> is the block diagonal matrix with Ω<sub>''I''</sub>'s on the diagonal. Then, since {{nowrap|<math display="inline">\det(I - t\frac\Omega{2\pi i}) = \det(I - t\frac{\Omega_1}{2\pi i}) \wedge \dots \wedge \det(I - t\frac{\Omega_m}{2\pi i})</math>,}} we have:
:<math>c_t(E) = c_t(E_1) \cdots c_t(E_m)</math>
where on the right the multiplication is that of a cohomology ring: [[cup product]]. For the normalization property, one computes the first Chern class of the [[complex projective line]]; see [[Chern class#Example: the complex tangent bundle of the Riemann sphere]].

Since <math>\Omega_{E \otimes E'} = \Omega_E \otimes I_{E'} + I_{E} \otimes \Omega_{E'}</math>,<ref>Proof: By definition, <math>\nabla^{E \otimes E'}(s \otimes s') = \nabla^{E} s \otimes s' + s \otimes\nabla^{E'} s'</math>. Now compute the square of <math>\nabla^{E \otimes E'}</math> using Leibniz's rule.</ref> we also have:
:<math>c_1(E \otimes E') = c_1(E) \operatorname{rank} (E') + \operatorname{rank}(E) c_1(E').</math>

Finally, the [[Chern character]] of ''E'' is given by
:<math>\operatorname{ch}(E) = [\operatorname{tr}(e^{-\Omega/2\pi i})] \in H^*(M, \Q)</math>
where <math>\Omega</math> is the curvature form of some connection on ''E'' (since <math>\Omega</math> is nilpotent, it is a polynomial in <math>\Omega</math>.) Then ch is a [[ring homomorphism]]:
:<math>\operatorname{ch}(E \oplus F) = \operatorname{ch}(E) + \operatorname{ch}(F), \, \operatorname{ch}(E \otimes F) = \operatorname{ch}(E) \operatorname{ch}(F).</math>
Now suppose, in some ring ''R'' containing the cohomology ring <math>H^*(M, \Complex)</math>, there is the factorization of the polynomial in ''t'':
:<math>c_t(E) = \prod_{j=0}^n (1 + \lambda_j t)</math>
where <math>\lambda_j</math> are in ''R'' (they are sometimes called Chern roots.) Then <math>\operatorname{ch}(E) = e^{\lambda_j}</math>.

== Example: Pontrjagin classes ==
If ''E'' is a smooth real vector bundle on a manifold ''M'', then the ''k''-th [[Pontrjagin class]] of ''E'' is given as:
:<math>p_k(E) = (-1)^k c_{2k}(E \otimes \Complex) \in H^{4k}(M; \Z)</math>
where we wrote <math>E \otimes \Complex</math> for the [[complex vector bundle|complexification]] of ''E''. Equivalently, it is the image under the Chern–Weil homomorphism of the invariant polynomial <math>g_{2k}</math> on <math>\mathfrak{gl}_n(\R)</math> given by:
:<math>\operatorname{det}\left(I - t {x \over 2 \pi}\right) = \sum_{k = 0}^n g_k(x) t^k.</math>
<!-- mention Euler class -->

== The homomorphism for holomorphic vector bundles ==
Let ''E'' be a [[holomorphic vector bundle|holomorphic (complex-)vector bundle]] on a complex manifold ''M''. The curvature form <math>\Omega</math> of ''E'', with respect to some hermitian metric, is not just a 2-form, but is in fact a (1, 1)-form (see [[holomorphic vector bundle#Hermitian metrics on a holomorphic vector bundle]]). Hence, the Chern–Weil homomorphism assumes the form: with <math>G = \operatorname{GL}_n(\Complex)</math>,
:<math>\Complex[\mathfrak{g}]_k \to H^{k, k}(M; \Complex), f \mapsto [f(\Omega)].</math>
